audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for imperial dating, John wilderness ministry, Isaiah citation, fruits of turning, ethical instruction, Messiah expectation, baptism of Jesus, voice, and genealogy.

verses.restored: In the fifteenth year of the rule of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate governing Judea, Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip tetrarch of Iturea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,

familiar.text: Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judaea, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of Ituraea and of the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias the tetrarch of Abilene,

modern.text: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, while Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, Herod tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip tetrarch of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,

original.text: Ἐν ἔτει δὲ πεντεκαιδεκάτῳ τῆς ἡγεμονίας Τιβερίου Καίσαρος, ἡγεμονεύοντος Ποντίου Πιλάτου τῆς Ἰουδαίας, καὶ τετρααρχοῦντος τῆς Γαλιλαίας Ἡρῴδου, Φιλίππου δὲ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ τετρααρχοῦντος τῆς Ἰτουραίας καὶ Τραχωνίτιδος χώρας, καὶ Λυσανίου τῆς Ἀβιληνῆς τετρααρχοῦντος,

verses.restored: during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of the Divine came upon John son of Zechariah in the wilderness.

familiar.text: Annas and Caiaphas being the high priests, the word of God came unto John the son of Zacharias in the wilderness.

modern.text: during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John son of Zechariah in the wilderness.

original.text: ἐπὶ ἀρχιερέως Ἅννα καὶ Καϊάφα, ἐγένετο ῥῆμα θεοῦ ἐπὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν Ζαχαρίου υἱὸν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ.

verses.restored: He went into all the region around the Jordan, proclaiming a baptism of turning/realignment for release of sins/misalignments.

familiar.text: And he came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins;

modern.text: He went into all the region around the Jordan, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins,

original.text: καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς ⸀πᾶσαν περίχωρον τοῦ Ἰορδάνου κηρύσσων βάπτισμα μετανοίας εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν,

verses.restored: As it has been written in the scroll of the words of Isaiah the prophet: A voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.

familiar.text: As it is written in the book of the words of Esaias the prophet, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.

modern.text: as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet: “A voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him.

original.text: ὡς γέγραπται ἐν βίβλῳ λόγων Ἠσαΐου τοῦ ⸀προφήτου· Φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ· Ἑτοιμάσατε τὴν ὁδὸν κυρίου, εὐθείας ποιεῖτε τὰς τρίβους αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Every ravine will be filled, every mountain and hill will be made low, the crooked will become straight, and the rough ways smooth.

familiar.text: Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low; and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough ways shall be made smooth;

modern.text: Every valley shall be filled in, and every mountain and hill made low. The crooked ways shall be made straight, and the rough ways smooth.

original.text: πᾶσα φάραγξ πληρωθήσεται καὶ πᾶν ὄρος καὶ βουνὸς ταπεινωθήσεται, καὶ ἔσται τὰ σκολιὰ εἰς ⸀εὐθείαν καὶ αἱ τραχεῖαι εἰς ὁδοὺς λείας·

verses.restored: All flesh will see the salvation of the Divine.

familiar.text: And all flesh shall see the salvation of God.

modern.text: And all humanity will see God’s salvation.’”

original.text: καὶ ὄψεται πᾶσα σὰρξ τὸ σωτήριον τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: He said to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him, Offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?

familiar.text: Then said he to the multitude that came forth to be baptized of him, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?

modern.text: Then John said to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him, “You brood of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?

original.text: Ἔλεγεν οὖν τοῖς ἐκπορευομένοις ὄχλοις βαπτισθῆναι ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ· Γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, τίς ὑπέδειξεν ὑμῖν φυγεῖν ἀπὸ τῆς μελλούσης ὀργῆς;

verses.restored: Therefore make fruits worthy of turning/realignment, and do not begin to say among yourselves, We have Abraham as father; for I say to you that the Divine is able from these stones to raise children to Abraham.

familiar.text: Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance, and begin not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, That God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.

modern.text: Produce fruit, then, in keeping with repentance. And do not begin to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that out of these stones God can raise up children for Abraham.

original.text: ποιήσατε οὖν καρποὺς ἀξίους τῆς μετανοίας· καὶ μὴ ἄρξησθε λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Πατέρα ἔχομεν τὸν Ἀβραάμ, λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι δύναται ὁ θεὸς ἐκ τῶν λίθων τούτων ἐγεῖραι τέκνα τῷ Ἀβραάμ.

verses.restored: Even now the axe is laid to the root of the trees; every tree not making beautiful/good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire.

familiar.text: And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: every tree therefore which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.

modern.text: The axe lies ready at the root of the trees, and every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.”

original.text: ἤδη δὲ καὶ ἡ ἀξίνη πρὸς τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν δένδρων κεῖται· πᾶν οὖν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.

verses.restored: The crowds asked him, What then shall we do?

familiar.text: And the people asked him, saying, What shall we do then?

modern.text: The crowds asked him, “What then should we do?”

original.text: Καὶ ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ ὄχλοι λέγοντες· Τί οὖν ⸀ποιήσωμεν;

verses.restored: He answered them, The one having two tunics must share with the one having none, and the one having food must do likewise.

familiar.text: He answereth and saith unto them, He that hath two coats, let him impart to him that hath none; and he that hath meat, let him do likewise.

modern.text: John replied, “Whoever has two tunics should share with him who has none, and whoever has food should do the same.”

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ⸀ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ὁ ἔχων δύο χιτῶνας μεταδότω τῷ μὴ ἔχοντι, καὶ ὁ ἔχων βρώματα ὁμοίως ποιείτω.

verses.restored: Tax collectors also came to be baptized and said to him, Teacher, what shall we do?

familiar.text: Then came also publicans to be baptized, and said unto him, Master, what shall we do?

modern.text: Even tax collectors came to be baptized. “Teacher,” they asked, “what should we do?”

original.text: ἦλθον δὲ καὶ τελῶναι βαπτισθῆναι καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν· Διδάσκαλε, τί ⸀ποιήσωμεν;

verses.restored: He said to them, Collect nothing more than what has been appointed to you.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Exact no more than that which is appointed you.

modern.text: “Collect no more than you are authorized,” he answered.

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Μηδὲν πλέον παρὰ τὸ διατεταγμένον ὑμῖν πράσσετε.

verses.restored: Soldiers also asked him, And we, what shall we do? He said to them, Extort from no one, accuse no one falsely, and be content with your wages.

familiar.text: And the soldiers likewise demanded of him, saying, And what shall we do? And he said unto them, Do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely; and be content with your wages.

modern.text: Then some soldiers asked him, “And what should we do?” “Do not take money by force or false accusation,” he said. “Be content with your wages.”

original.text: ἐπηρώτων δὲ αὐτὸν καὶ στρατευόμενοι λέγοντες· ⸂Τί ποιήσωμεν καὶ ἡμεῖς⸃; καὶ εἶπεν ⸀αὐτοῖς· Μηδένα διασείσητε μηδὲ συκοφαντήσητε, καὶ ἀρκεῖσθε τοῖς ὀψωνίοις ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: As the people were waiting expectantly and all were reasoning in their hearts about John, whether he might be the Messiah,

familiar.text: And as the people were in expectation, and all men mused in their hearts of John, whether he were the Christ, or not;

modern.text: The people were waiting expectantly and were all wondering in their hearts if John could be the Christ.

original.text: Προσδοκῶντος δὲ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ διαλογιζομένων πάντων ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν περὶ τοῦ Ἰωάννου, μήποτε αὐτὸς εἴη ὁ χριστός,

verses.restored: John answered all, saying, I baptize you with water, but one stronger than I is coming; I am not worthy to loosen the strap of his sandals. He will baptize you in holy Spirit and fire.

familiar.text: John answered, saying unto them all, I indeed baptize you with water; but one mightier than I cometh, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to unloose: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire:

modern.text: John answered all of them: “I baptize you with water, but One more powerful than I will come, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.

original.text: ἀπεκρίνατο ⸂λέγων πᾶσιν ὁ Ἰωάννης⸃· Ἐγὼ μὲν ὕδατι βαπτίζω ὑμᾶς· ἔρχεται δὲ ὁ ἰσχυρότερός μου, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς λῦσαι τὸν ἱμάντα τῶν ὑποδημάτων αὐτοῦ· αὐτὸς ὑμᾶς βαπτίσει ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ πυρί·

verses.restored: His winnowing fork is in his hand to clear his threshing floor, to gather the wheat into his storehouse, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire.

familiar.text: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and will gather the wheat into his garner; but the chaff he will burn with fire unquenchable.

modern.text: His winnowing fork is in His hand to clear His threshing floor and to gather the wheat into His barn; but He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.”

original.text: οὗ τὸ πτύον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ ⸀διακαθᾶραι τὴν ἅλωνα αὐτοῦ καὶ ⸀συναγαγεῖν τὸν σῖτον εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην αὐτοῦ, τὸ δὲ ἄχυρον κατακαύσει πυρὶ ἀσβέστῳ.

verses.restored: So with many other exhortations he announced good news to the people.

familiar.text: And many other things in his exhortation preached he unto the people.

modern.text: With these and many other exhortations, John proclaimed the good news to the people.

original.text: Πολλὰ μὲν οὖν καὶ ἕτερα παρακαλῶν εὐηγγελίζετο τὸν λαόν·

verses.restored: But Herod the tetrarch, being rebuked by him concerning Herodias, his brother's wife, and concerning all the harmful things Herod had done,

familiar.text: But Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him for Herodias his brother Philip’s wife, and for all the evils which Herod had done,

modern.text: But when he rebuked Herod the tetrarch regarding his brother’s wife Herodias and all the evils he had done,

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἡρῴδης ὁ τετραάρχης, ἐλεγχόμενος ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ περὶ Ἡρῳδιάδος τῆς γυναικὸς τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ καὶ περὶ πάντων ὧν ἐποίησεν πονηρῶν ὁ Ἡρῴδης,

verses.restored: added this also to them all: he shut John in prison.

familiar.text: Added yet this above all, that he shut up John in prison.

modern.text: Herod added this to them all: He locked John up in prison. The Baptism of Jesus (Matthew 3:13–17; Mark 1:9–11; John 1:29–34)

original.text: προσέθηκεν καὶ τοῦτο ἐπὶ πᾶσιν, ⸀καὶ κατέκλεισεν τὸν Ἰωάννην ⸀ἐν φυλακῇ.

verses.restored: Now when all the people were baptized, and Jesus also had been baptized and was praying, heaven was opened,

familiar.text: Now when all the people were baptized, it came to pass, that Jesus also being baptized, and praying, the heaven was opened,

modern.text: When all the people were being baptized, Jesus was baptized too. And as He was praying, heaven was opened,

original.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ βαπτισθῆναι ἅπαντα τὸν λαὸν καὶ Ἰησοῦ βαπτισθέντος καὶ προσευχομένου ἀνεῳχθῆναι τὸν οὐρανὸν

verses.restored: and the holy Spirit descended upon him in bodily form like a dove, and a voice came from heaven: You are my beloved Son; in you I delight.

familiar.text: And the Holy Ghost descended in a bodily shape like a dove upon him, and a voice came from heaven, which said, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.

modern.text: and the Holy Spirit descended on Him in a bodily form like a dove. And a voice came from heaven: “You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.” The Genealogy of Jesus (Ruth 4:18–22; Matthew 1:1–17)

original.text: καὶ καταβῆναι τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον σωματικῷ εἴδει ⸀ὡς περιστερὰν ἐπʼ αὐτόν, καὶ φωνὴν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ⸀γενέσθαι· Σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν σοὶ εὐδόκησα.

modern.text: Jesus Himself was about thirty years old when He began His ministry. He was regarded as the son of Joseph, the son of Heli,
